items.text: CUET (PG) 2026 is a common computer-based entrance test for postgraduate admission at Central Universities and other participating universities and institutions for the 2026-27 session.
items.note: Page numbers for this Information Bulletin are PDF page numbers; the printed page number is one less.

items.text: The Ministry of Education and UGC have given NTA the job of conducting CUET (PG). The test was introduced in 2022.
NTA only registers candidates, conducts the test, publishes and finalises answer keys, declares results and hosts score cards. Merit lists are prepared by the participating universities.
Questions about admission, merit lists or counselling must go to the university concerned, not to NTA.
In 2026, 4,11,366 unique candidates registered and 3,45,220 appeared. The test covered 157 subjects in 50 shifts.
Candidates who have passed a Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or who are in the final year and appearing in 2026, can take CUET (PG) 2026.
There is no age limit for the test. Check the age rule of the university you are applying to.
Each university's own rules apply on qualification, subject combinations, quota, category, relaxation, age and reservation. Check the university website.
Taking the test does not guarantee admission. The candidate must also meet the university's programme-wise eligibility.
Reservation for OBC-NCL, Gen-EWS, SC and ST follows Government of India rules, but each participating university applies its own reservation policy. NTA has no role in this.
Eligible PwD/PwBD candidates get compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour, and a scribe if they opted for one in the application.
items.note: Information Bulletin, PDF page 5, and the 05 March 2026 advisory.

items.text: Mode: Computer Based Test (CBT) only.
A candidate can choose up to four question paper codes, matching the codes each university has mapped to its programmes.
Each paper has 75 multiple-choice questions and lasts 90 minutes.
Marking: +4 for a correct answer, -1 for a wrong answer, 0 for an unanswered question or one only marked for review.
If more than one option is correct, +4 goes to anyone who marked any correct option. If no option is correct, or a question is wrong or dropped, every candidate who appeared gets +4.
items.note: Continues on PDF page 11.

items.text: Most papers are bilingual (English and Hindi). Language papers are in that language (Linguistics in English only). M.Tech/Higher Sciences papers are in English only. Acharya papers are in Sanskrit, except Hindu Studies (English and Hindi) and Indian Knowledge System and Baudha Darshan (English, Hindi and Sanskrit).
If the language versions differ, the English version counts, except for language papers and Acharya papers.
items.note: The 05 March 2026 advisory (https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20260305173937.pdf, page 8) says the Sanskrit version counts for Acharya papers.

items.text: In 2026, the exam ran in 2-3 shifts a day: 09:00-10:30 AM, 12:30-2:00 PM and 4:00-5:30 PM.
Calculators are not allowed in any form.
A question that is answered and also marked for review is evaluated.
CUET (PG) 2026 had 157 subjects (question paper codes).
Paper groups: Common (COQP01-22), Languages (LAQP01-41), Science (SCQP01-30), Humanities (HUQP01-26), M.Tech/Higher Sciences (MTQP01-12) and Acharya (ACQP01-26).
items.note: Appendix II, PDF pages 32-35. We counted the codes: 22 + 41 + 30 + 26 + 12 + 26 = 157.

items.text: Common papers include: General (COQP11), General - Management (COQP12), Commerce (COQP08), Economics (COQP10), LL.M. (COQP14), M.Ed. (COQP15), Mass Communication and Journalism (COQP17), Library and Information Science (COQP13) and several B.Ed. papers.
Different universities may test similar courses under different paper codes (for example, Hindu Studies). The candidate is responsible for choosing the right code.
Syllabi are published by domain (Science, M.Tech, Language, Humanities, Common, Acharya) on the CUET (PG) syllabus page.
Each university's programmes, their mapped paper codes and eligibility are on the participating-universities page.
Applications are made online only, at https://exams.nta.nic.in/cuet-pg/. Only one form per candidate, and one mobile number and email per form.
Step 1, registration: fill in details, set a password and a security question, and note the Application Number the system generates.
Step 2, application form: personal details, test papers, exam cities and qualifications; capture a live photo and upload a scanned photo, signature and PwD certificate if applicable.
Uploads: photo 10-200 KB JPG/JPEG (colour or black-and-white, 80% face with ears visible, no mask, white background); signature 10-50 KB JPG/JPEG; disability/UDID certificate 50-300 KB PDF.
items.note: The PDF size rule is on PDF page 7.

items.text: If the photo or signature is blurred or unclear, the application is rejected and cannot be corrected later.
Step 3, fee payment: pay online by net banking, card or UPI. Processing charges and GST are extra.
The confirmation page appears only after successful payment; download and keep it. A form without completed payment is rejected.
items.note: The rejection rule is on PDF page 8.

items.text: Exam city choices must be in the state/UT of the permanent or present address. Up to four cities may be chosen.
items.note: The Information Bulletin (PDF page 16) says up to TWO cities. The 19 Dec 2025 notice and FAQ 13 (FAQ PDF page 2) allow up to four.

items.text: Category certificates are not uploaded. Instead, enter the certificate number, date of issue and issuing authority, and show the certificate during admission.
items.note: Continues on FAQ page 3.

items.text: Correction window (2026): mobile number, email, address, photo and signature cannot be changed. Only one of candidate, father or mother name can be changed. Exam cities, date of birth, gender, category, PwBD status, paper codes and (for non-Aadhaar registrants) Aadhaar details can be changed.
Corrections can be made only once. Changes that raise the fee need extra payment, and reducing the number of papers gets no refund.
The application fee cannot be refunded or transferred, and a submitted form cannot be cancelled.
items.note: The cancellation rule is FAQ 25, on page 3.

items.text: Foreign national candidates (OCI/PIO) enter 111111 as the PIN code. Documents from DigiLocker are accepted, and an APAAR ID is not required.
General: ₹1400 for up to two papers, plus ₹700 for each extra paper.
Gen-EWS / OBC-NCL: ₹1200 for up to two papers, plus ₹600 for each extra paper.
SC / ST / Third Gender: ₹1100 for up to two papers, plus ₹600 for each extra paper.
PwD / PwBD: ₹1000 for up to two papers, plus ₹600 for each extra paper.
Exam centres outside India: ₹7000 for up to two papers, plus ₹3500 for each extra paper, whatever the category.
items.note: The 'whatever the category' rule is on PDF page 6.

items.text: Bank or payment-gateway charges and GST are paid on top of the exam fee.
Correcting the form costs nothing extra unless the category or the number of papers changes.
2026 cycle, as first announced: registration 14 December 2025 to 14 January 2026 (11:50 PM); fee payment by 14 January 2026; correction 18-20 January 2026; exam in March 2026.
items.note: These were later extended (see the next items).

items.text: 2026 cycle, first extension: application and fee payment to 20 January 2026; correction 23-25 January 2026.
items.note: Replaced by the 20 January 2026 extension.

items.text: 2026 cycle, second extension: application to 23 January 2026; fee payment to 25 January 2026; correction 28-30 January 2026 (11:50 PM).
items.note: The 14 February 2026 notice says registration ran 14 Dec 2025 to 25 Jan 2026, and gives the correction window as '28 to 30 January 2025', which looks like a typo for 2026.

items.text: 2026 cycle: exam scheduled for 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, 18, 19, 24, 25 and 27 March 2026, in 44 shifts of 90 minutes.
items.note: The subject-wise date sheet is in Annexure I of the same notice (pages 2-4).

items.text: 2026 cycle: city intimation slips came out in phases: 26 Feb (for 06-07 Mar), 01 Mar (08-10 Mar), 05 Mar (11-13 Mar) and 12 Mar (16-27 Mar).
items.note: Taken from the notice titles on nta.ac.in (Notice_20260301232424, Notice_20260305170853, Notice_20260312121956).

items.text: 2026 cycle: admit cards came out in phases: 03 Mar (for 06-10 Mar), 07 Mar (11-13 Mar), 12 Mar (16-19 Mar) and 18 Mar (24-27 Mar).
items.note: Taken from the notice titles on nta.ac.in (Notice_20260307183610, Notice_20260312214849, Notice_20260318205101).

items.text: 2026 cycle: a special rescheduled exam on 29-30 March 2026 was held for 534 candidates from Tura (Meghalaya) and 31 candidates from overseas centres, in 28 subjects.
2026 cycle: provisional answer keys could be challenged from 11 to 14 April 2026; the fee had to be paid by 14 April 2026, 10:00 AM.
2026 cycle: results were declared on 24 April 2026.
2027 (tentative): NTA's revised exam calendar lists CUET (PG) on 02-05, 08-09, 12, 15-19, 24-25 and 29-31 March 2027 (17 days). These dates may change.
items.note: Revised calendar notice of 26 Oct 2026: https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20261026114247.pdf. The earlier calendar of 16 Sep 2026 (https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20260916195948.pdf, page 2) listed 01-05, 08, 12-20 and 24-25 March 2027, with buffer days 30-31 March. The revised calendar replaces it.

sections.title: City intimation slip and admit card

items.text: The exam city intimation slip is released about ten days before the exam; log in to download it. It is not the admit card.
items.note: The 26 Feb 2026 notice also says the slip is not the admit card.

items.text: The e-Admit Card is issued provisionally on https://exams.nta.nic.in/cuet-pg/ and must be downloaded with your login. It is not sent by post or email.
Receiving an admit card does not mean your eligibility has been accepted. The university checks it later.
If you cannot download the admit card, or its details are wrong, call 011-40759000 (10 AM - 5 PM). Take the exam with the downloaded card; NTA will correct its records later.
Candidates taking subjects on more than one day must bring a separate admit card for each day.
items.note: Continues on page 3.

items.text: The allotted exam centre, city and timing cannot be changed.
Reach the exam centre about 90 minutes before the exam starts. No one is let in after the gate closes.
items.note: The gate-closing rule is in the 05 March 2026 advisory (https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20260305173937.pdf, page 1).

items.text: Candidates who did not register through Aadhaar should report at least 1 hour before the gate closes, for identity verification.

Must carry: a printed e-Admit Card with the self-declaration (A4); a passport photo (same as uploaded); a simple transparent ball-point pen; an original valid photo ID; a PwBD certificate if claiming relaxation; and a name-change document if the name has changed.
items.note: The 05 March 2026 advisory asks for at least two passport photos.

items.text: Accepted photo IDs (bulletin): university/college ID, PAN, driving licence, voter ID, passport, Aadhaar or e-Aadhaar with photo, ration card with photo, bank passbook with photo. Photocopies or ID images on a phone are not accepted.
items.note: The 05 March 2026 advisory (page 1) lists government-issued IDs and also accepts an Aadhaar enrolment number with photo. It is also the source of the photocopy rule.

items.text: Do not bring personal belongings, electronic devices or mobile phones. There is no place to store them at the centre.
Diabetic candidates may carry sugar tablets, fruit and a transparent water bottle, but not packed food.
Keep your Aadhaar biometrics unlocked on exam day, for biometric verification. After a toilet break, frisking and biometrics are repeated.
Do rough work only on the sheets provided. Write your name and roll number on each sheet and drop them in the box before leaving.
You may not leave the hall before the exam ends, and you cannot re-enter once you leave.
There is no re-test for candidates who miss their scheduled exam for any reason.
Unfair means follow the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. They include carrying prohibited items, impersonation, using electronic devices and tampering with documents.
Exam centres are under CCTV surveillance and fitted with jammers.
NTA posts the provisional answer keys and question papers with recorded responses on https://exams.nta.nic.in/cuet-pg/ with a public notice, usually for two to three days.
Challenging an answer costs ₹200 per question. The fee is paid online and is not refunded.
items.note: The same fee is in the Information Bulletin (PDF page 22) and FAQ 45.

items.text: Only paid challenges made through the 'key challenge' link within the time window are considered. Challenges without justification are rejected.

Steps: log in with Application Number and password or date of birth, open 'View Answer Sheet', choose the option IDs you claim, upload proof as one PDF, submit, then pay. Claims cannot be changed after payment.
Dropped questions are highlighted and cannot be challenged.
Subject experts review all challenges. Candidates are not told individually whether their challenge was accepted. Results are prepared from the final answer key.
Final answer keys for CUET (PG) 2026 are published subject-wise on the CUET (PG) website.
CUET (PG) 2026 results were declared on 24 April 2026. Score cards are downloaded from the website using Application Number and date of birth; they are not posted.
items.note: Information Bulletin, PDF page 23.

items.text: The 2026 score card is also available on DigiLocker. You need an Aadhaar-linked DigiLocker account, your CUET PG registration number and roll number, and the exam year.
items.note: Notice dated 28 April 2026.

items.text: Bulletin rule: for papers planned across several shifts, raw marks are converted to an NTA score using percentile-based normalisation.
items.note: The method is in Appendix V (PDF page 45 onward).

items.text: For 2026, NTA said results were prepared on actual marks. The small group in the 29-30 March rescheduled exam was not normalised against the main group, because a statistical comparison would not be meaningful.
items.note: This clarification (14 June 2026) differs from the bulletin's general normalisation rule.

items.text: There is no re-evaluation or re-checking of results.
The CUET (PG) 2026 score is valid only for admissions in academic year 2026-27.
Scores and candidate data are shared with participating universities. Each university runs its own counselling and prepares its own merit list.
A complaint about the result is considered only if raised within 30 days of the result. Disputes fall under Delhi/New Delhi jurisdiction.
In 2026 there were 7,14,621 subject registrations and 5,04,301 subject appearances.
The official list is on the CUET (PG) site in four groups: Central; State; Government Institutions / Fully Funded; and Deemed / Private.
198 universities took part in CUET (PG) 2026: 45 Central, 40 State Government, 24 Government Institutions and 89 others (Private and Deemed).
items.note: When fetched on 2026-11-12, the website lists had the same 198 rows (45 / 40 / 24 / 89).

items.text: The list changes over time; check the NTA and CUET (PG) websites for updates.
CUET (PG) help desk: email helpdesk-cuetpg@nta.ac.in; phone 011-40759000 or 011-69227700.
items.note: The Information Bulletin (PDF page 5) and FAQ 51 list 011-40759000.

items.text: NTA general help desk: genadmin@nta.ac.in; phone 011-69227700 or 011-40759000.
Official websites: https://exams.nta.nic.in/cuet-pg/ and https://nta.ac.in.
Legal notices and petitions can be served on NTA only at legal@nta.ac.in.
NTA's address on notices from September/October 2026 is 5th Floor, Government of India Press Building, Minto Road, New Delhi - 110002.
items.note: The 2026 CUET (PG) notices show the older address: First Floor, NSIC-MDBP Building, Okhla Industrial Estate, New Delhi - 110020. NTA posted a 'Relocation of NTA Office' notice on 15 September 2026 (https://nta.ac.in/Download/Notice/Notice_20260915113220.pdf).

unknown: No CUET (PG) 2027 Information Bulletin has been published as of 2026-11-12. Application dates, fees, the correction window, and city slip, admit card and result dates for 2027 are not announced.
The only 2027 information is NTA's tentative exam calendar (March 2027), which may change. NTA has not confirmed it with a CUET (PG) 2027 notice.
We cannot tell whether the 2027 pattern (75 questions, 90 minutes, +4/-1, up to 4 papers, 157 codes) or the fees will change.

We captured only the titles of these notices, not their contents: 10 Jan and 16 Jan 2026 (application advisories), 01 Mar, 05 Mar, 12 Mar (city slips), 07 Mar, 12 Mar, 18 Mar (admit cards) and 13 Apr 2026 (answer-key advisory). Most are scanned images.
The Information Bulletin (two exam cities) and the 19 Dec 2025 notice and FAQ (four cities) disagree. We recorded the later four-city rule and noted the conflict.
The official list of participating universities does not give each university's state, so the state column in universities-CUET_PG.csv is empty.
Dates of PG notices we did not open come from the timestamp in NTA's file name.
